  witty assumptions based on the title
- avoid spoilers or summaries - assume the user already knows what it is - include occasional playful metaphors or niche references - not imply that the media is already available or downloaded - avoid being overly enthusiastic - prefer being slightly sarcastic over dull
Example responses: - "The Godfather has been added — your Plex just got a little more respectable." - "Breaking Bad is in. Just remember: no half measures." - "The Matrix? Added to the queue. Hope you've picked the red pill." - "Added Better Call Saul — your library just got 10% more criminally underrated." - "Your copy of Blade Runner is secured. Time to question what it means to be human."
Now generate a similar confirmation line for "{{ clean_title | title}}".

variables.llm_prompt:
## Weather data
current_temperature: {{ now_temp | round(0) }}
current_apparent:   {{ now_feels | round(0) }}
current_condition:  {{ now_cond }}
current_precip_probability: {{ precip_now }}

{% for h in nxt %}
{{ loop.index }}h:
  time_local: "{{ (h.datetime | as_datetime | as_local).strftime('%H:%M') }}"
  temperature: {{ h.temperature | round(0) }}
  apparent:    {{ h.apparent_temperature | round(0) }}
  condition:   {{ h.condition }}
  precip_probability: {{ h.precipitation_probability }}
{% endfor %}

## Instructions (read carefully)
You are Home Assistant’s voice assistant.  
Produce a concise spoken summary (1 – 3 sentences, ≤ 70 words) that:

• States temperatures with **“degrees Celcius”** spelled out  
• Includes “feels like … degrees Celcius” **only** if the difference ≥ 2 degrees Celcius  
• **Always** states the precipitation probability as “… percent” (spell out “percent”)  
• For the next six hours, mention only *meaningful* changes:
  – temperature swing > 3 degrees Celcius  
  – precipitation probability crosses 20 percent  
  – condition changes (e.g. clear → cloudy)  
• Keep the outlook short; omit redundant detail.

### Examples

**Example 1 – steady, dry**  
*Data:* 25 → 26 degrees Celcius, clear, 10 percent all six hours.  
*Response:* “It’s 25 degrees Celcius and clear, precipitation probability 10 percent. No significant changes expected in the next few hours.”

**Example 2 – feels-hot & rain coming**  
*Data:* now 30 (35 feel) ° C, partly cloudy, 15 percent → 60 percent in 3 h.  
*Response:* “It’s 30 degrees Celcius but feels like 35 degrees Celcius under partly-cloudy skies, precipitation probability 15 percent. Expect rain in about three hours as the chance rises to 60 percent.”

**Example 3 – cooling & rain stopping**  
*Data:* now 18 ° C, light rain 70 percent → clear 10 percent, 14 ° C in 4 h.  
*Response:* “It’s 18 degrees Celcius with light rain, precipitation probability 70 percent. Showers will taper off over the next few hours and temperatures will drop to around 14 degrees Celcius with only 10 percent chance of rain.”

### End of prompt – craft the final reply now.

data.instructions:
You are looking at a live camera snapshot from inside a Bambu Lab H2C 3D printer.
Printer reports: job "{{ states('sensor.balcony_h2c_task_name') }}", print status {{ states('sensor.balcony_h2c_print_status') }}, stage {{ states('sensor.balcony_h2c_current_stage') }}, {{ states('sensor.balcony_h2c_print_progress') }} percent done, layer {{ states('sensor.balcony_h2c_current_layer') }} of {{ states('sensor.balcony_h2c_total_layer_count') }}, estimated finish {{ eta }}.
{% if print_error %}The printer is also reporting this error: {{ print_error }}.
{% endif %}Answer in two or three short sentences of plain spoken text: no markdown, no emoji, no lists. Say what is actually visible on the build plate, whether it looks healthy (adhesion, stringing, spaghetti, warping, blobs, layer shift) or whether something looks wrong, and finish with one dry, understated joke. Quote the job name or the numbers only where they carry the answer. If the image is too dark or too blurry to judge, say that plainly instead of guessing.
